biography: Maksim Orlov's journey began not on a grand prix circuit, but on the frozen lakes surrounding his small Russian hometown. As a child, he spent countless hours building makeshift ice racers with his father, a former mechanic. The thrill of controlled chaos, the dance on the edge of grip, ignited a passion that would define his life. He began karting at 14, quickly establishing himself as a tenacious competitor, known for his unwavering defense and calculated overtakes. Transitioning to the Kart 2-Stroke 125cc Direct series, Orlov faced fierce competition. One defining moment came at the 2018 Moscow Grand Prix Karting, where, despite starting in 15th position after a qualifying mishap, he relentlessly fought his way through the pack to secure a podium finish. Now at 29, Orlov is considered to be in his prime, a seasoned veteran known for his strategic brilliance, seeking to cement his legacy in the world of kart racing.
drivingStyle: Orlov is a master of defensive driving. He rarely makes rash decisions, preferring to patiently observe his opponents and capitalize on their mistakes. In corners, he favors a late-braking approach, positioning his kart precisely to block overtaking attempts. He is known for his exceptional tire management, often conserving his rubber in the early stages of a race to unleash a devastating attack in the final laps. Under pressure, Orlov remains calm and collected, his experience allowing him to make calculated decisions even in the most intense situations.

rivalries.name: Dimitri Volkov
rivalries.reason: A long-standing rivalry stemming from their early karting days, fueled by numerous on-track collisions and accusations of unsportsmanlike conduct.

rivalries.name: Irina Petrova
rivalries.reason: A strategic rivalry, as Irina is a notoriously aggressive overtaker. Orlov finds her style dangerous and unpredictable, leading to frequent clashes.

rivalries.name: Sergei Markov
rivalries.reason: A purely professional rivalry. Markov is known for his raw speed, forcing Orlov to push his defensive driving to its absolute limit.

quirks: Always wears the same worn-out pair of racing gloves, claiming they bring him good luck.
Before each race, he listens to a specific classical music piece to center his focus.
Meticulously cleans his kart's steering wheel with a microfiber cloth before every session.
famousQuote: "Racing isn't about speed; it's about control. Control of the kart, control of your emotions, control of the race."
careerHighlight: Winning the 2020 St. Petersburg Karting Championship after a nail-biting final race where he defended his lead against relentless pressure from Dimitri Volkov.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out on the first lap of the 2017 European Karting Championship, after a mechanical failure sent him spinning into the barrier, resulting in a season-ending injury.
